tiers.label: Pilot (one brand, 3 markets)
tiers.description: Proof of value on one brand: brief-to-broadcast for 2-3 campaigns with holdout testing.

tiers.label: One brand (6 markets)
tiers.description: A full brand team in production use with Guardian, rights and approvals.

tiers.label: Global portfolio (12 markets) - reference customer
tiers.description: Contoso Consumer Brands at full adoption: multi-brand, 12 markets, 50,000 versions a year.

tiers.label: Agency network (multi-tenant, ~30 client brands)
tiers.description: A holding company or agency network running client brands in isolated tenants on one platform.

tiers.label: Enterprise scale (catalog + generative video + personalization)
tiers.description: A larger global consumer group or retailer (several times the reference customer) with a large catalog: 150,000 approved versions a year, 20 markets, 1,000 users, 40,000 SKUs, personalised variants at 10x, generative video on part of the hero and adapted spots, and a marketing data and clean-room platform on Fabric. Expansion levers E1-E4 are all at full scale.

portfolio.note: Illustrative sales-motion assumptions (not a forecast or a commitment): pilots last 12 months and convert into the one-brand tier counts.

tam.note: Directional ceiling = target accounts x steady-state tier run-rate; assumption-driven (account counts are not sourced), not a forecast.

expansion.note: Enterprise-scale accounts run at the enterprise-scale tier instead of the global-portfolio tier; a share of the remaining global-portfolio accounts adds E1-E4 at the reference customer's own scale. Assumption-driven, not a forecast.

e1.label: E1 · Generative video (VideoProvider)
e1.description: Generative video through the pluggable VideoProvider (Azure OpenAI video models where deployable in the customer's region, or partner video models from the Foundry catalog): generated footage for hero masters and adapted videos, billed per generated second, behind the same Guardian, provenance and approval gates. The demo ships the ffmpeg compositor.

e2.label: E2 · Catalog-scale product content
e2.description: Catalog-scale product content: product-page images, lifestyle scenes, alt-text and localized descriptions for SKUs x markets x images, fed by PIM / e-commerce connectors and checked by the Guardian.

e3.label: E3 · Audience-level personalization
e3.description: Audience-level personalization: pre-generated segment variants (5-20x more versions per campaign) managed by the variant engine and measured by segment.

e4.label: E4 · Marketing data & clean-room platform (Fabric)
e4.description: Marketing data and clean-room platform on Microsoft Fabric: performance data plus CRM / CDP, measurement models and clean-room collaboration, beyond the minimal data pull-through already in the core model.

reference_customer_path.label: Global portfolio + E1-E4 at full scale (reference customer, steady state)

reference_customer_expanded_tier.label: Global portfolio + E1-E4 at full scale (reference customer, steady state)
reference_customer_expanded_tier.description: Contoso Consumer Brands at full adoption: multi-brand, 12 markets, 50,000 versions a year.

video_price_reference.availability: Azure OpenAI Sora 2 (preview on Microsoft Learn); region availability varies; sora-2 deprecated in swedencentral as of Nov 2026

video_price_reference.meter: Sora 2 pro high res glbl Second

video_price_reference.availability: Foundry catalog partner model; verify availability, terms and ACR eligibility

video_price_reference.meter: Fal MM H3 Mx Trb Im-Vd 1080 Video

notes: Base and Conservative keep every lever off, so their numbers are the Release-1 campaign studio only; Upside switches all four on at full scale. The 'full_expansion_case' block shows any scenario with E1-E4 at full scale.

Honest reading: generated video and catalog images are cheap per unit at list price (cents per image, dollars per kept second), so E1 and E2 add little Azure consumption at this customer's volumes even though their customer benefit is large; the consumption that makes ACR material comes from the data platform (E4), segment-scale personalization (E3), and from customer breadth and users (the enterprise-scale tier).

Video is billed per generated second, including rejected takes, so cost per kept second equals list price x takes. Sora 2 is a preview model on Microsoft Learn and is deprecated in swedencentral as of Nov 2026: the VideoProvider plug-in keeps the product independent of any single video model.

Partner video models ('Azure Fal' meters, effective 2026-11-01) are listed in the Retail Prices API at about US$0.03-0.30 per second; they are shown as a price reference only. Confirm availability, terms and ACR eligibility with Microsoft before relying on them.

pricing_basis.billing: Pay-as-you-go list price (priceType=Consumption); no EA/MACC discount, reservations or savings plans
pricing_basis.region: swedencentral (global meters for Front Door, Translator and Private Link); westeurope list prices are within a few percent

unit_economics.note: Azure cost per approved version = bottom-up list-price consumption divided by approved versions; agency cost = production + agency fees + rework + localisation pool divided by today's asset count. Campaign-scale studio only: expansion levers E1-E4 are reported separately (acr.expansion).

Paid media in scope of testing
Expansion levers E1-E4 (off to full scale)
